reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Wednesday in late October. Nothing is on fire. Nothing is spectacular. You woke up, you made coffee, you went to work, and tonight you'll come home to the same apartment you left this morning. For a lot of us, this used to be the hardest kind of day to stay sober through — not the crisis, not the celebration, just the middle of a week in the middle of a month when nothing much is happening.

I used to think a good life was built out of highlights. Trips, parties, big nights. What I've learned in eleven years is that the highlights are the easy part. The life gets built on Wednesdays. On the unremarkable walk to the car with leaves on the ground. On making dinner instead of ordering it. On the phone call you make because you said you would. The texture of a real life is almost entirely made of these small, forgettable moments — and sobriety is what lets you actually be in them instead of enduring them until something better comes along.

Durant wasn't talking about recovery, but he could have been. You don't become someone you can live with in a single decision. You become that person on Wednesdays. Today counts. Not because it's special, but because it isn't.
reflection.meditation: Sit for two minutes. Notice one small thing about today — the light, the temperature, the sound outside — that you'd have been too checked out to register five years ago. Let that be enough.

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days, and today is one of them.
I can be present for this Wednesday without needing it to be more than it is.
I trust the small choices I'm making — they are becoming who I am.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for an unremarkable day I get to remember. Grateful for the quiet it took years to earn — a mind that isn't negotiating with itself before noon, a phone that isn't full of apologies to send. Grateful for the people who stayed, and the ones I've met since who only know this version of me. Grateful that today, I'm not fighting myself.
gratitude.closing: One more Wednesday. One more day I get to keep.
